criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. A test on a scratch repository with several nested files under records/ imports them. The importer's self-check passes. The new commit on athena/records has every records/ file at the same path with the same blob id. It also holds import-manifest.json.
criteria.evidence: I ran the test: full_import_passes_self_check_and_copies_every_file ... ok. It builds 5 files under records/, including nested ones and a binary file, plus a README.md outside records/. It asserts that RECORDS_REF equals the returned commit, that the commit's ls_tree minus the manifest equals C0's records/ path→oid map, that the manifest is present, and that the commit has no parents.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. The manifest parses as HistoryRecord::ImportManifest and validates. It lists each source path with its blob id at C0 and the SHA-256 of its contents. The entry count equals the file count at C0.
criteria.evidence: I ran the test: manifest_lists_each_path_with_blob_and_sha256 ... ok. It parses the manifest with HistoryRecord::parse into the ImportManifest variant and calls validate(). It asserts c0 == C0 and paths.len() == the source count. For each entry it checks the blob_id against C0's oid and the sha256 against an independent sha256_hex of the bytes.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. The self-check fails with a distinct error for each of three cases: a file missing from the imported commit, a file whose bytes changed, and an extra file not in C0. A count mismatch is also covered. A passing import is not what proves these.
criteria.evidence: I ran the tests and all passed. self_check_fails_on_missing_file returns Missing{records/top.md}. self_check_fails_on_changed_file returns BlobMismatch{records/top.md}. self_check_fails_on_extra_file returns Extra{records/extra.json}. self_check_fails_on_count_mismatch returns CountMismatch{the manifest,5,6}. Hash and blob tampering in the manifest and a missing manifest are also covered. control_untampered_import_passes shows the same path without tampering returns Ok.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. A second import into a repository that already has the records branch is refused, and the branch tip is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: I ran the tests: second_import_is_refused_and_tip_unchanged ... ok. It asserts AlreadyImported{tip==first}, that RECORDS_REF is still first, and that rev-list has length 1. an_existing_unrelated_records_branch_blocks_the_import ... ok, with the tip unchanged.

criteria.criterion: No existing caller, CLI command, job pipeline step or workflow invokes the importer, and nothing is run against this repository's main. The diff touches no athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows file. The importer module docs say the importer is not wired in.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat lists only the 8 deliverable files: no athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow file. A Grep for records_import, import_records and verify_import finds hits only in records_import.rs itself, the `pub mod` line and a doc line in athena-core lib.rs, doc comments in athena-git, the design doc and the CHANGELOG. The module's '# Status' section says it is not wired in and has not been run against main.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. All pass, and the importer reuses RecordsWriter and ImportManifest rather than reimplementing them.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records show fmt passed, clippy with -D warnings passed, and tests passed (1053 tests). The code calls RecordsWriter::new(git).append(...) and builds athena_data::history::ImportManifest and ImportedPath. It reuses athena_data::sha256_hex, and has no update-ref or commit-tree plumbing of its own.

criteria.criterion: The design doc's job-2 status text and the CHANGELOG say the importer exists and is not yet run against main, and a reader can see where the code lives.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The design doc adds '**Built (build job 2, §10 item 2).**', which names crates/athena-core/src/records_import.rs and says it is tested on scratch repositories only, not wired in, and has not yet been run against main. The CHANGELOG's Added entry names the same path and makes the same statement.

findings.summary: When the self-check fails, the bad commit stays on athena/records, so any later import is refused with AlreadyImported and the import cannot simply be retried.
findings.evidence: writer.append runs before verify_import, and the module docs say 'the commit stays on the branch'. This is documented and follows from the append-only rule, but the cutover (job 7) should know to run the importer into a scratch repository first, as §10 item 2 already advises.

findings.summary: The CountMismatch check on the imported commit can never trigger in practice, because the Missing and Extra checks run first. Only the count check on the manifest is reachable.
findings.evidence: The loops over source.keys() and imported.keys() return Missing or Extra before the count loop runs, so 'the imported commit' count can only match. It is harmless as defence in depth.

summary: The change adds the job-2 importer as `crates/athena-core/src/records_import.rs`, and it does what the request and docs/design/records-history.md §4 item 2 and §10 item 2 ask. It copies every file under records/ at C0 into one orphan commit on athena/records, using `RecordsWriter::append`. It writes import-manifest.json as an `ImportManifest` that lists each path, its blob id and its SHA-256. It then re-reads the commit and fails, with a distinct error for each case, on a missing file, an extra file, a changed blob, a wrong hash or a count mismatch. It refuses a second import and leaves the branch tip unchanged. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`: all 15 tests passed, including tests that tamper with the import to prove each failure case, and a control test where the untampered import passes. Athena's fmt, clippy and test records pass. Nothing calls the importer: the only references are its own module, the `pub mod` line, doc comments and the docs. All 8 changed files are on the expected deliverables list. One minor note: when the self-check fails, the bad commit stays on the append-only branch, so a later import is refused and cannot simply retry. The module docs say this openly.
